title: Equilibrium and missing forces
target: Find a missing force when acceleration is zero.
criteria: Recognize rest and constant velocity as possible equilibrium.
Find missing forces from a zero net-force condition.
Explain why turning is not equilibrium.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: Which motion can have zero net force?
cpa.guide: Equilibrium requires zero acceleration, not necessarily rest.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A crate remains stationary throughout an observed interval. In an inertial frame, what is its net force during that interval?
options: Unknown solely because its mass is large.
Equal to its weight downward with no other forces.
cpa.guide: Constant zero velocity means zero acceleration and net force.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A sign weighs 45 N and hangs at rest from one vertical cable. What is tension?
cpa.guide: Vertical equilibrium requires tension to balance weight.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A resting object has 19 N right and 7 N left plus one unknown horizontal force. What must that force be?
cpa.guide: 19 − 7 = 12 N right must be balanced by 12 N left.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Why is a car turning at steady speed not in equilibrium?
options: Its speed is zero at every turn.
Every moving object is out of equilibrium.
Its changing velocity direction requires nonzero acceleration.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A rider at the top of a circular ride has balanced vertical forces claimed in a diagram, yet follows a curved path with inward acceleration. What should be checked?
options: Balanced forces always produce circular motion.
The claimed force balance is inconsistent with the required inward net force.
The rider must have zero mass.
cpa.guide: If acceleration is inward, the net force cannot be zero.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
